The user wants to install a custom Groq adapter into their Paperclip instance: they ran `npm install git+https://github.com/acunningham-ship-it/groq-paperclip-adapter.git`. After that, they likely expect the adapter to be usable by an agent. I already listed the existing agents in the company (using the `/agents` endpoint) and saw four agents (Ideator, CEO, Coder, CTO) all using the `opencode_local` adapter. None of them are using the newly installed `groq-paperclip-adapter` yet.

My next step is to understand why the new adapter isn’t showing up. The adapter package was installed under the Paperclip instance’s `adapter-plugins` directory, specifically at `/home/lane/.paperclip/adapter-plugins/node_modules/groq-paperclip-adapter`. I need to see how this adapter reads its configuration and environment variables, because the user likely needs to set a `GROQ_API_KEY` or specify a model name. If the adapter expects certain config keys and they aren’t being passed, it won’t activate.

To diagnose this, I should inspect the source file that implements the server side of the adapter: `dist/server/index.js` inside the installed package. I want to know which configuration keys it looks for (e.g., `config...`, `env`, `GROQ_API_KEY`, `model`). A quick way is to grep for those patterns and count occurrences to see the most relevant terms. Then I’ll also look at the actual lines where those keys appear to understand the expected structure.

Thus, I’ll run a grep that extracts any occurrence of `config` followed by letters, the word `env`, the literal `GROQ_API_KEY`, or the word `model`. I’ll sort and count them to get a sense of prominence, then show the first few matching lines with line numbers for context. This should give me enough insight to advise the user on what config to add to an agent or environment variables to set.

Hence, the appropriate tool call is a Bash command that performs these greps on the adapter’s index.js file and outputs the summarized counts and sample lines.

arguments.command: grep -o "config[A-Za-z]*\|env\b\|GROQ_API_KEY\|model\b" -r /home/lane/.paperclip/adapter-plugins/node_modules/groq-paperclip-adapter/dist/server/index.js | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head; echo ===; grep -n "GROQ_API_KEY\|config\.\|model" /home/lane/.paperclip/adapter-plugins/node_modules/groq-paperclip-adapter/dist/server/index.js | head -40
